title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 2 of these notes studies 'algebraic homomorphisms' between groups P^i(X) of codimension-i cycles algebraically equivalent to zero. A homomorphism phi: P^j(X') -> P^i(X) is called algebraic if some multiple N·phi is induced by an algebraic correspondence on X×X'. The previous page reduced algebraic families Y(k) -> A^i_alg(X) to homomorphisms A(k) = P^{dim A}(A) -> P^i(X) from abelian varieties.

This page does three things.

(1) Inverses. It first poses a 'more subtle question': if an algebraic homomorphism is a group isomorphism, is its inverse also algebraic, i.e. induced by a correspondence up to a multiple?

(2) Duality for i+j = n+1, where n = dim X. Let A, B be abelian varieties put in perfect duality, so A ≅ B^* and B ≅ A^*. The claim is a natural bijection
Hom_alg(A, P^i(X)) ≅ Hom_alg(P^j(X), B).
The construction goes as follows.
- An algebraic homomorphism A -> P^i(X) is given by a cycle Z of codimension i on X×A.
- The transpose ^tZ acts as a correspondence from X to A. It sends codimension-j cycles on X to codimension (i+j-n) cycles on A.
- Since i+j-n = 1, this gives P^j(X) -> P^1(A) = Pic^0(A) = A^* ≅ B.
- Conversely, a correspondence W giving P^j(X) -> B transposes to Pic^0(B) = A -> P^i(X).
So P^i(X) behaves like a 'Picard-type' object (maps in from abelian varieties) and P^j(X) like an 'Albanese-type' object (maps out to abelian varieties). For i = 1, j = n this recovers the Pic^0 / Alb duality.

(3) The gap Grothendieck flags. One must check that P^j(X) -> B depends only on the homomorphism A -> P^i(X), not on the choice of cycle Z representing it. More generally he raises transposition in general: when do correspondences inducing the same map P^i(X) -> P^{i'}(X') induce the same transposed map P^{j'}(X') -> P^j(X)? 'Cf plus bas': the next page attacks exactly this with l-adic cohomology. There the statement is u_Z = 0 <=> a(^tZ) = 0 on H^{2(n-i)+1}(X)(n-i) -> H^1(A), proved by restricting to an ample curve C in A. He explicitly asks whether the converse holds.

Modern reading. This is the duality question for algebraic representatives / algebraic intermediate Jacobians in codimension i and n+1-i, phrased as a universal-property adjunction for regular homomorphisms in Samuel's sense.
errors: The bijection is asserted before well-definedness is established. Grothendieck notices this himself ('il faut vérifier...').

One direction of well-definedness is true. If u_Z = 0, then Z_* : H_1(A) -> H^{2i-1}(X) vanishes (Abel–Jacobi over C, or the l-adic analogue). So the transpose on H^{2j-1}(X) -> H^1(A) vanishes, since 2j-1 = 2n-2i+1. A map into an abelian variety induced by a correspondence is detected by this cohomological action, so ^tZ_* = 0 on P^j(X) -> B.

The reverse direction is the real problem. For the bijection one needs: two cycles W, W' inducing the same map P^j(X) -> B give the same map A -> P^i(X). This amounts to the converse in Theorem 3.1 of the next page. If P^i is taken modulo rational equivalence, it fails in general, or is at best expected only conditionally: there are homomorphisms from abelian varieties into Chow groups with trivial Abel–Jacobi image, e.g. Beauville-component constructions on A×S with p_g(S) > 0. So the bijection is only correct after passing to a coarser quotient, essentially the image in the algebraic representative.

Even at the level of algebraic representatives, the full duality Ab^i(X) ~ (Ab^{n+1-i}(X))^∨ (up to isogeny) is not known unconditionally in general. It is expected from the Lefschetz / generalized Hodge-type standard conjectures. The page treats it as essentially formal.
The previous page's reduction (a family = constant + homomorphism) is a theorem-of-the-cube-type statement. It is not valid for Chow groups mod rational equivalence. That issue is inherited here.

ideas.what: Algebraic homomorphisms between groups of cycles algebraically equivalent to zero, defined as homomorphisms induced (up to a multiple) by correspondences
ideas.modern_name: regular homomorphisms / homomorphisms induced by correspondences
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Samuel (1958–60), later Murre, H. Saito

ideas.what: Duality Hom_alg(A, P^i(X)) ≅ Hom_alg(P^{n+1-i}(X), A^*) via transposition of correspondences
ideas.modern_name: duality of algebraic representatives / algebraic intermediate Jacobians J_a^{2i-1} vs J_a^{2n-2i+1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Murre (algebraic representatives, 1983–85); Achter–Casalaina-Martin–Vial and Vial (duality questions, 2010s)

ideas.what: Question whether an algebraic homomorphism that is a group isomorphism has an algebraic inverse
ideas.modern_name: algebraicity of inverses of correspondence-induced isomorphisms (cf. Lefschetz-standard-conjecture-type inverses)
ideas.usually_credited_to: related to Grothendieck's standard conjectures (Lefschetz type B: inverse of Lefschetz isomorphism algebraic)
ideas.where_published: analogous question for cohomology in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969)

ideas.what: Whether the transposed action is well defined on cycles-modulo-equivalence (correspondences acting trivially one way act trivially transposed)
ideas.modern_name: transposition / compatibility of correspondences with Abel–Jacobi; Bloch–Beilinson-type questions

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (c. 1965) the duality between codimension-i and codimension-(n+1-i) algebraically trivial cycles as an adjunction-type bijection Hom_alg(A, P^i(X)) ≅ Hom_alg(P^{n+1-i}(X), A^*). He leaves its well-definedness open. This anticipates by ~20 years the duality questions for Murre's algebraic representatives.
missed.quote: alors il y a correspondance biunivoque entre Hom alg(A, P^i(X)) et Hom alg(P^j(X), B)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The duality of algebraic representatives Ab^i and Ab^{n+1-i} is still open in general. Grothendieck's adjunction phrasing is a clean way to state it and to isolate exactly which half needs Bloch–Beilinson-type input. This is mainly of historical interest, as the idea is known.

missed.claim: The question whether correspondence-induced isomorphisms of cycle groups have correspondence-induced inverses is a Chow-group analogue of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B. It is posed here and not pursued.
missed.quote: Une question plus subtile est s'ils peuvent s'inverser, quand ce sont des isomorphismes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is related to the existence of algebraic inverses for isomorphisms of algebraic representatives and of motives (e.g. conservativity). It is a known circle of ideas, but this early cycle-level formulation is undocumented.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early, private formulation of duality and transposition questions for algebraically trivial cycles. These later became the theory of regular homomorphisms and algebraic representatives (Murre, Saito, Achter–Casalaina-Martin–Vial). It is historically interesting as an anticipation, but the questions themselves are now standard. The page contains no finished result beyond the formal transposition construction.
transcription_corrections: 'accomplies' should read 'accouplées' (two abelian varieties paired by a perfect duality).
The marginal addition reads 'pour i+j = n+1' (attached to 'P^j(X)' replacing a struck-out superscript).
Target of ^tZ: 'P^{dim[?]-i}(A)' should read 'P^{i+j-n}(A) = P^1(A) ≅ B'.
The final lines read 'Question de transposition, et plus généralement, pour P^i(X) — P^{i'}(X') en P^{j'}(X') — P^j(X). Cf plus bas ....'
